title: Another Pontifical prayer asks the Father to make the held cross-sign a saving remedy and shield—implying God-given virtue in the material cross
source_text: XXVII. Ibidem est oratio ad Deum Patrem directa, in qua ab ipso petit Episcopus, ut signum crucis quod prae manibus habet, sit remedium salutare generi humano, & protectio ac tutela contra jacula inimicorum. Oratio his terminis concepta est, Rogamus te Domine sancte, Pater omnipotens, sempiterne Deus, ut digneris benedicere hoc signum crucis tuae, ut sit remedium salutare generi humano; sit soliditas fidei; perfectio bonorum operum; redemptio animarum; sit solamen & protectio ac tutela contra saeva jacula inimicorum, &c. Quam orationem qui ad Deum habent, si fidant se exaudiri, necesse est ut credant, istam lapideam, vel metallicam crucem exinde a Deo habere virtutem, per quam hominibus procurare possit varias benedictiones, tum temporales, tum spirituales, contra quam definit Synodus Tridentina. Nam alioqui quomodo dici posset, illam factam fuisse, ut petit oratio, remedium humano generi salutare, & tutelam contra saeva inimicorum jacula?
pass_a_gloss: In the same place there is a prayer directed to God the Father, in which the Bishop asks of Him that the sign of the cross which he has in hand may be a saving remedy for the human race, and protection and guard against the darts of enemies. The prayer is conceived in these terms: We ask You, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, that You would deign to bless this sign of Your cross, that it may be a saving remedy for the human race; may it be the solidity of faith; the perfection of good works; the redemption of souls; may it be comfort and protection and guard against the fierce darts of enemies, etc. Which prayer those who offer to God, if they trust they are heard, must believe that that stone or metal cross thence has from God a virtue by which it can procure for men various blessings, temporal and spiritual—against which the Tridentine Synod defines. For otherwise how could it be said that it was made, as the prayer asks, a saving remedy for the human race and a guard against the fierce darts of enemies?
pass_b_english: A second Pontifical prayer asks the Father to make the held cross a saving remedy and shield.
If the prayer is trusted, the material cross must be thought to receive real virtue from God—Trent’s denial notwithstanding.

lemmas.gloss: against which the Tridentine Synod defines

choices.why: Virtue is ascribed to the consecrated artifact.
